clues: These old stone ruins stand in southern Mexico, near a wide river. Thick jungle trees once grew over them and hid them from sight for years.
This place is warm and damp, with huge rains. More than two metres of rain falls here in a single year.
Long ago, this was a proud Maya city-state. It faded and fell in the eighth century, and the jungle then grew over its stones.
Its best known king was Pacal the Great. His tomb was found in the Temple of the Inscriptions.
Search for tall roof combs and fine carved panels on its stone temples. They are among the best works the Maya ever made, and they mark this site at once.
